key_insight: CUA failures follow a long-tail: a small set of rare, complex GUI interactions causes a disproportionate share of errors. Generating diverse synthetic examples and measuring coverage with a dedicated benchmark can close this data gap and improve reliability.
problem_solved: Mitigates the scarcity of training/evaluation data for complex, low-frequency on-screen interactions that make computer-use agents brittle and untrustworthy in real-world tasks.
method: Analyze failure logs from advanced CUAs to expose a long-tail distribution of GUI operations and identify high-impact rare interactions.
Design a synthetic data-generation pipeline that produces diverse, multi-step and edge-case GUI action sequences to augment rare classes.
Create and release a benchmark that quantifies coverage of the human action space and evaluates model robustness on long-tail interactions.
impact: Provides practitioners with a practical route to reduce brittle failures in automation agents by expanding rare-action training data and standardizing evaluation; improves trustworthiness and real-world readiness of CUAs.
visual_elements: Long-tail bar chart: action frequency vs failure contribution (highlight rare actions causing most failures)
End-to-end pipeline diagram: failure analysis → synthetic data generation → model training → benchmark evaluation
Coverage heatmap of the human action space showing dense vs sparse regions and where synthetic data fills gaps
Annotated UI sequence examples showing original failure case and synthesized variants that address it
paper_title: Covering Human Action Space for Computer Use: Data Synthesis and Benchmark
paper_authors: Miaosen Zhang, Xiaohan Zhao, Zhihong Tan, Zhou Huoshen, Yijia Fan
